acceptance: A request to any of the 98 /api route files whose Host is not a literal loopback authority, whose Origin is not http(s)://<Host>, or whose Sec-Fetch-Site is not absent, same-origin or none gets 403 {"error":"Same-host requests only"} from server.js before Next is invoked (all route classes: public read, private read, form write, JSON write, delete, credential, multiplayer, e2e hook).

The same rule judges every WebSocket upgrade (multiplayer socket, HMR path, any other) before the path or bearer is read: a foreign Origin or rebinding Host gets 403; a same-host client still reaches the existing bearer check.
Encoded, doubled-slash, dot-segment, backslash, upper-case, absolute-form and undecodable spellings of /api are guarded; page routes are not (ruling 7).
Requests with no Origin and no Fetch Metadata are still served (same-host controls).

The rule lives once in src/lib/api/sameHostGuard.ts; local-seats, token and unlock call it first, before the method check, body parse, rate limit and KDF; local-seats behaviour and error text are unchanged and its existing suite passes unchanged.
server.js exits 1 at boot when tsx or the guard cannot load; a failure after boot answers an API request 500 and destroys an upgrade, never admitting either unguarded (ruling 2).
The one WebSocketServer refuses an inbound frame larger than 1 MiB: exactly 1,048,576 bytes accepted and 1,048,577 closed with 1009 on the match and campaign channels.

scripts/validate-multiplayer-packaged-socket.mjs exports assertSameHostGuard and main() calls it on the built, unflagged server (rebinding-Host read 403, cross-site form 403 with no identity created, same-host read 200, foreign-Origin upgrade 403). Not wired into CI here (DESKTOP-GUARDS-1).
No session, cookie, rate-limit or error-text change; extraction preserves local-seats behaviour.

Scaling a reconcile frame to 1000 damaged units gives 110494 bytes, and the largest campaign scenario pack serialised as a proposal is 29096 bytes. At 108.74 bytes per unit a reconcile frame needs about 4812 units to reach 512 KiB. Nothing exceeds 512 KiB, so there is no stop for Root. Synthetic boundary probes (1 MiB, 1 MiB + 1, 95 MiB) are kept apart and are not client-built frames.

rulings20261028.R2: A missing tsx or guard is fatal at boot (exit 1 before the ready marker); a later load failure fails closed with 500. Disclosed below, including the Electron Startup Error Retry/Quit behaviour. Rows for both were ADDED to the candidate routes test at this admission (candidateAmendment).
rulings20261028.R3: Caps are per merge diff (A2M and B precedent): 15 files / 500 counted additions, tests and evidence line-exempt but file-counted, no deletion credit, no new exemption. Measured with the validator's own UNCOUNTED_FILES patterns. The validator has no merge-diff file cap for ordinary units, so there is no conflict; the file count is exactly 15 with the generated page counted (zero slack).
rulings20261028.R4: Realistic inbound frames were measured before the freeze (frameMeasurement). The largest realistic frame is far below 512 KiB, so no stop for Root.
rulings20261028.R5: Accepted for later: an Electron-as-node packaged validator run with --standalone-dir on a post-merge build is this unit's mainProof. Installer rehearsal is Step 8.
rulings20261028.R6: Admission after PR C, rebased on fetched main 3dc706ed4. No old baseline or prep count is represented as current: every number in this receipt was measured at the baseline.
rulings20261028.R7: /api HTTP routes and every upgrade are guarded as registered. Page and _next asset rebinding reads are a disclosed limitation. No scope expansion.
rulings20261028.R8: The packaged validator stays a manual gate until DESKTOP-GUARDS-1. It is not added to STEP2-RC-RERUN-1.
rulings20261028.accounting: This standalone admission is Step 4 PR 1; the implementation is PR 2; the closure, carrying the CAMPAIGN-LIVE-WRITE-1 admission, is PR 3. Three of 29. L1-SMOKE-B's closure already merged (#2352) and cannot carry this admission.

limitations: Fatal boot (ruling 2): if tsx or the guard cannot load, server.js logs "[mp-boot] same-host guard unavailable" and exits 1 before it prints the ready marker. In the packaged app the embedded-server wrapper rejects with "The embedded server exited before it was ready (code 1, signal null)" (desktop/electron/main.server.ts:39) and the window shows the Startup Error dialog "MekStation could not start its local server." with Retry and Quit (desktop/electron/main.window.ts:281-298). Retry restarts the server; with a permanently missing tsx or guard the dialog returns on every attempt, and Quit closes the app. Until now only the guard-free multiplayer runtime load was non-fatal (server.js:540 logs "[mp-boot] runtime load failed" and keeps serving Next without multiplayer); the guard is the first thing that makes tsx fatal for the whole app.

Later load failure (ruling 2): loadSameHostGuard() caches a successful load, so only a failure inside the guard call can happen after boot. An HTTP request then reaches the existing catch and is answered 500 "Internal Server Error", never handed to Next; an upgrade reaches the existing catch and the socket is destroyed without a handshake (no 500 status line, no 101). Both are rows of the candidate test.

Page routes and _next assets (ruling 7): a DNS-rebinding page can still read HTML pages and _next assets (rebinding reads of pages are not judged). Only /api and upgrades are. Every upgrade is judged, including the dev HMR path.

dev:e2e (next dev --webpack) bypasses server.js: that lane has the guard only on the three credential routes (local-seats, multiplayer/auth/token, vault/identity/unlock). No workflow or script uses it (package.json, a comment in scripts/qc/run-flow-audit.mjs, a test fixture).

Requests with no Origin and no Fetch Metadata (Electron main, curl, Node, Playwright request) stay admitted (owner decision 2026-10-25 item 8): a local process can still call the API; the guard stops browser-mediated attacks only.

The packaged validator is a manual gate until DESKTOP-GUARDS-1 (ruling 8). Its main() call of assertSameHostGuard is exercised only by a packaged run (survivor-by-construction, not a mutant); the non-vacuity rows prove the checker itself against fake servers.

Server-entry rows run the real server.js, real ws and real tsx with next, the multiplayer runtime modules and SQLite stubbed by a Module._load preload (technique of validate-multiplayer-packaged-socket.test.ts). Real Next dev (HMR, compile of a refused route), Playwright, the hydrated image and the packaged Electron run are NOT proven here; the e2e-smoke CI job is the only proof of real Next dev.

The 1 MiB cap is a product decision, not a measured margin: CampaignProposal.proposal is z.unknown on the wire schema and nothing on the server bounds it below the cap. maxPayload limits received messages only; outbound snapshots and replay chunks are not affected.
Node's own fetch and WebSocket send no Origin and no Sec-Fetch-Site (probed on Node 24.15 in the prep refresh, not re-run on 22.22 here); the frozen L1 harness requests are plain loopback.

S7-09 (unthrottled vault sign route), S5-06 and B15-AUTH-LIMIT stay outside this unit. No session, cookie, rate-limit or error-text redesign. B15-AUTH-ORIGIN is absorbed by annotation; B15-1 keeps its operator session scope.
On Windows a raw HTTP upgrade client with the default keep-alive agent loses every second refusal to ECONNRESET; the candidate tests use agent:false. Test hazard, not a product bug.
